the ionospheric TEC variability is strongly affected by the solar cycle and the local time, and the annual and semiannual variations have distinct trends for the daytime and nighttime.

the first two modes contain 80–85% of the total variability of global TEC maps and the variability is strongly dependent on the local time, the solar condition, and the season.

the solar irradiance is the main driving factor of ionospheric variability, and the local time is a crucial parameter that affects ionospheric variability.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PCA analysis of the global ionosphere is able to reveal the main ionospherical variability under different solar conditions.
the ionosphere is more variable in the early morning and late afternoon, and the variability is less in the daytime.
the PCA technique is an effective tool to extract and analyze the variability of the ionosphere, and the results can be utilized to improve the accuracy of ionospheric modeling and forecasting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the variability of the ionosphere is a complex process that is not only related to the solar cycle but also to the local time of the ionosphere.
the ionosphere exhibits distinct temporal and spatial variability under different solar conditions.
, in addition to the solar cycle, the local time of observation is another important factor that should be taken into consideration in the study of the ionosphere variability on a global level.
